bug_semantics: An EventStream subscriber was authorized only at dashboard-subscription granularity, then placed in a global client registry. OnExecutionStarted, OnExecutionFinished, and OnOutputChunk iterated that registry and sent every execution event to every subscriber without applying acl.IsAllowedLogs for the recipient and action. The finished-event LogEntry included the command's accumulated Output, while OutputChunk exposed live bytes, so a low-privileged authenticated dashboard user could observe metadata and output for an action whose logs that user was not authorized to view.
flaw_origin: Commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 introduced the ConnectRPC EventStream path itself in service/internal/api/api.go and proto/olivetin/api/v1/olivetin.proto. In that same commit, EventStream registered a user-bearing client globally; OnExecutionStarted, OnExecutionFinished, and OnOutputChunk broadcast to every registered client; and internalLogEntryToPb copied logEntry.Output into the response. The immediate parent had no ConnectRPC EventStream implementation. This was a new independently vulnerable transport path, not merely the later movement of already-vulnerable lines: a legacy WebSocket broadcaster existed separately and was later ACL-fixed by 4e7273b616245d60626b51a291edd97ab8ef53bc without touching service/internal/api/api.go, leaving the EventStream path vulnerable.
ai_marker: absent: the raw commit object for a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 names author and committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, has message 'chore: OliveTin 3k progress', and contains no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool, or bot trailer/identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/security/advisories/GHSA-228v-wc5r-j8m7 identifies service/internal/api/api.go EventStream, OnExecutionStarted, OnExecutionFinished, OnOutputChunk, and internalLogEntryToPb; its PoC on tag 3000.10.2 shows an ACL-less alice receiving an admin-started protected action's ExecutionFinished output.

git grep at a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 locates internalLogEntryToPb at service/internal/api/api.go:228, the Output assignment at :236, EventStream at :485, OnExecutionStarted at :524, OnExecutionFinished at :540, and OnOutputChunk at :565. The a62d58 diff creates service/internal/api/api.go and the EventStream RPC and sends each of those execution payloads by iterating connectedClients, with no recipient/action ACL predicate.

Immediate-parent verification: git grep for EventStream, OnExecutionStarted, OnExecutionFinished, and OnOutputChunk at d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0 over service/internal/api/api.go and proto/olivetin/api/v1/olivetin.proto returns no matches; service/internal/api/api.go does not exist in that parent tree. git cat-file commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 confirms d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0 is its sole immediate parent.

git log -L over EventStream shows fcd3ccc59a58b41fe7b1a545610910d2154983f9 later added checkDashboardAccess only before registration, preserving the missing per-action recipient check. The separate legacy WebSocket fix 4e7273b616245d60626b51a291edd97ab8ef53bc added acl.IsAllowedLogs in service/internal/httpservers/websocket.go but did not modify the vulnerable ConnectRPC EventStream file.

Version membership: git tag --contains a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 begins with 3000.0.0, and git merge-base a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 3000.10.2 returns the introducer itself, proving the reported/tested 3000.10.2 tag contains the flaw. The bundle's normalized '< 3000.10.2' / first-patched 3000.10.2 fields conflict with its own advisory prose and the current first-party page, which says 3000.10.2 is affected and lists no patched version.

Direct fix https://github.com/OliveTin/OliveTin/commit/acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc adds mayViewExecutionEvent/isLogEntryAllowed recipient checks before started, finished, and output-chunk delivery. git merge-base with tag 3000.11.2 is b298a6bd8caadd8a69eeb731771f5ac659b9e237 rather than the fix, while git merge-base with 3000.11.3 returns acd6cb839e999bb2b0e9a91424f51e88be3f7ffc; git tag --contains the fix begins at 3000.11.3. Thus repository history establishes the effective patched release boundary despite stale advisory package metadata.

BIC-only AI check: git cat-file commit a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404 shows tree aad57bab656ffb103468611f332652e5f5bd070c, sole parent d4fe9eaa793f508f44bc60f0a1109cb008a6a5b0, human author/committer jamesread <contact@jread.com>, and only the subject 'chore: OliveTin 3k progress'; there are no trailers or bot identities. The commit is a direct single-parent repository commit with no reconstructable squash members, so no decomposition is claimed.
reasoning: The vulnerable lifecycle starts with a62d58f11955fe192f45da13e23ba996a2759404, which creates the affected ConnectRPC EventStream implementation and, in the same smallest history object, combines global subscription with unconditional fan-out of action events and output. Its parent lacks that path and all of the vulnerable functions, so parent absence is directly established. A later coarse dashboard gate changed who could subscribe but did not make delivery action-aware; a legacy WebSocket ACL correction affected a different file/path and therefore did not cure this EventStream. Tag ancestry puts the introducer before every 3000 release, including the advisory's demonstrated 3000.10.2, and puts the ACL-filtering fix in 3000.11.3 but not 3000.11.2. The raw BIC commit object has only a human author/committer and no AI attribution marker. Under the protocol's BIC-only attribution rule, the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
